questions.subject: FILM_STUDIES
questions.learningObjective: Define and distinguish key film studies concepts
questions.stem: Which statement best defines Cinematography?

options.text: It is the art of capturing images on camera through choices of framing, lens, movement, and exposure.
It is the position of the camera relative to its subject, shaping apparent power and perspective.
It is the motion of the camera during a shot, such as a pan, tilt, dolly, or track.
It is how much of the scene the image includes and how the subject is bounded by the edges.

questions.explanation: It is the art of capturing images on camera through choices of framing, lens, movement, and exposure. This is precisely what Cinematography means; the alternatives describe Camera angle, Camera movement, Framing, which are different ideas.
questions.hint: Recall the specific meaning of Cinematography.

questions.stem: Which claim about Framing is accurate?

options.text: It is the art of capturing images on camera through choices of framing, lens, movement, and exposure.
It is the position of the camera relative to its subject, shaping apparent power and perspective.
It is the motion of the camera during a shot, such as a pan, tilt, dolly, or track.
It is how much of the scene the image includes and how the subject is bounded by the edges.

questions.explanation: It is how much of the scene the image includes and how the subject is bounded by the edges. This is precisely what Framing means; the alternatives describe Cinematography, Camera angle, Camera movement, which are different ideas.
questions.hint: Recall the specific meaning of Framing.
